Subject: RFP question: availability measurement, telemetry & crediting methodology

Jonas —

Thanks for the RFP response so far. Procurement has a few clarifying questions specific to the availability and latency sections before we move to contracting:

1) Please confirm the exact availability definition you will accept for the enterprise contract (example: endpoint-level boolean health, synthetic vs. real-traffic, p95/p99).
2) How are measurement windows defined (calendar month vs. rolling 30-day)?
3) What telemetry will be provided as evidence (retention period, sampling, access method — CSV, dashboard, API)?
4) How are service credits calculated (formula, caps, exclusions for planned maintenance and force majeure)?
5) If Orion requests an audit, what is the evidence-hand off and expected timeline?

We need precision here because internal finance will tie service credits to our vendor risk model. Can you respond with a proposed, contract-ready wording and any supporting artifacts you can attach?

Best,

From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: RFP question: availability measurement, telemetry & crediting methodology

Linda —

Thanks, and good questions. Below is a proposed contract-ready summary and the evidence we typically provide. I attached a short PDF that defines each metric and shows a worked example of credit calculations. If you want any wording tightened for legal, we can do that in-line.

Proposed availability & measurement summary (draft contract language):
- Availability ("Uptime"): percentage of calendar month minutes during which the Redwood API control plane and the customer-assigned serving endpoints respond with 200-series HTTP status to accepted health probes. Measurement basis: combined synthetic probes (internal) plus sampled production traffic (1% uniform sampling across regions), aggregated per-minute.
- Latency: 95th percentile (p95) of end-to-end generation latency for successful requests (2xx) measured over the same sampling population; customer can request p99 as an optional add-on. Latency excludes cold-start windows (first 60s after model deploy), and excludes known maintenance windows.
- Measurement window: default is calendar month; we can also support rolling 30-day windows on request for enterprise customers.
- Service credits: monthly credit equals max(0, (SLO_target - Observed_Availability) / SLO_target) * Monthly_Service_Fee, capped at 25% per month. Example in attached PDF.
- Exclusions: planned maintenance (>=72h notice) and force majeure; customer-specific network outages (when our telemetry shows 100% success from our egress to backend but customer network reports failure) are excluded.
- Evidence & retention: raw minute-level availability and sampled latency time-series (CSV export) retained for 13 months; a PDF summary with percentiles and probe counts provided within 5 business days of a credit request. For audits, we will provide access to a read-only dataset export and redacted logs as permitted by policy (timeline 10 business days).

Attachments: SLA_Metrics_Definitions_v1.pdf (definitions, worked examples).

If that looks reasonable I can circulate an internal recommendation for concession boundaries (credit tiers, whether we accept p99 by default) and come back with a single redline for legal.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
(Attachment: SLA_Metrics_Definitions_v1.pdf)

Subject: Fwd: RFP question: availability measurement, telemetry & crediting methodology

Looping you both in — Linda from Orion pushed back asking for 'contract-ready wording' and explicit telemetry hand-off. My draft is below (sent to Linda).

Quick internal points for trade-offs:
- They specifically asked whether we'll accept rolling 30-day vs. calendar month. Offering both is okay; prefer calendar month as default.
- Service credit cap: 25% / month seems standard. We should consider a 12-month cumulative cap (recommended: 50%) to limit long-tail exposure for enterprise deals.
- Measurement population: 1% sampling of production traffic + synthetic probes is how we reduce token cost for metrics. Procurement may try to require full-population p99 which we need to push back on.

Karthik — if we were to include p99, we should offer it as an opt-in at a 20% premium or as part of a higher-tier SLO with reduced credit multiplier. Can you advise on operational feasibility for p99?

On the evidence side: we can provide CSV exports for minute-level availability and a prebuilt 'evidence playbook' that walks procurement through how to interpret the data and reconcile with their telemetry. I attached a stub playbook for you to review.

—Jonas

Linda —

Appreciate the clarity on your side. Per our internal review, please find consolidated, contract-ready language and materials below (and attached). Key items: 

1) Finalized summary (for SLA exhibit):
- Uptime target: 99.9% monthly availability (as defined below). Measured using combined synthetic probes and a 1% uniform sample of production requests, aggregated into per-minute availability datapoints. Default window: calendar month; rolling 30-day measurement allowed by request.
- Latency: p95 measured over same sampled population. p99 available as optional add-on (see below).

2) Crediting matrix (monthly):
- Observed >= 99.9%: no credit
- Observed 99.0% – 99.9%: 5% credit
- Observed < 99.0%: 15% credit (capped at 25% of monthly invoice for extraordinary events)

3) Measurement specifics / exclusions:
- Exclude planned maintenance (>=72h notice), force majeure, and verified customer-side network outages.
- Cold-start exclusion: first 60s after a model deploy or restart.

4) Evidence, retention & audit:
- We will provide: minute-level availability CSV export (timestamp, probe_count, success_count, region, endpoint), sampled-latency TSV (per-request sample id, latency_ms, status_code), and a summary PDF with percentiles and counts. Retention: 13 months.
- Evidence delivery: standard credit request -> summary PDF within 5 business days; audit exports (redacted logs) within 10 business days. If Orion requests a real-time API stream or direct access, support can be provided under a separate telemetry subscription.

5) p99 / telemetry add-ons:
- p99 SLO and full-population telemetry available as an enterprise add-on. Requirements: 14-day notice, telemetry fee to cover storage/export, and a short onboarding window for instrumentation (we will share an onboarding checklist).

Attachments: SLA_Metrics_Definitions_v1.pdf, evidence-playbook.docx.

If this aligns with your procurement team's needs, can we schedule a 30-minute call Wednesday to finalize the SLA exhibit and confirm the crediting matrix?

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
